reviews.body: Pros: Doormen staff are awesome, view is great, apartments are good size, laundry in building. Cons: Management not always responsive, some laundry machines are more recently not operational on regular basis. Heating is expensive.

Pros: Full service building
Newer building Cons: Flooded multiple floors previously
Leaks are common

Pros: The building is great. No pests, great garbage disposal, great doormen. Nice view if you get a unit facing Manhattan. Cons: Far from the subway, although the bus and ferry are close by. The park across the street gets VERY loud, with parties going until 3-4am in the summer.

Pros: The doorman crew is the best part of the building. Cons: Poor insulation in the walls and balcony doors are not sealed. Cold air comes through and causes heating bills to skyrocket in the winter. Management does nothing to help.
Pros: Doormen lovely as is the super. They are beautiful apts with a gorgeous view Cons: Management company is awful and lie. Two major floods in two years.

Pros: The available parking and mini-splits in each unit are nice. Cons: Management is impossible to reach for problems until suddenly they decide to respond. Their super is no where to be found and doesn't answer his phone but sure takes up space with his G wagon in the parking lot. They promise all new tenants amenities that will NEVER be built. No community room, gym, bike storage etc have been completed in over 4 years. Management is shady about how they sign leases - they just show up a week after the due date with a physical  stack of papers, don't send you a copy, and rumor has it they use this to sue tenants who annoy them. (Check the litigation history.) If you rent here, you'll get paper thin walls with noisy, nasty neighbors that flood the (nonsmoking) building with weed smoke. Leaks from rainwater are a massive problem here, as is energy efficiency. The building received an "F" energy rating and your ConEd bill will reflect that. A single bedroom might be charged as high as $700 in the summer.

Pros: Rent is cheaper than other places. That’s it Cons: Management sucks
General upkeep is horrible
Neighborhood is ghetto
No amenities or anything when a gym and rooftop deck was supposed to be built

Pros: The apartment itself is relatively new and looks nice. Big windows and my unit had a decent view of the RFK bridge. The unit itself comes with a fairly new fridge/freezer, dishwasher, gas oven and stove, microwave, a washer and dryer, and air conditioning/heat split units. 

The kitchen had a decent amount of counter space thanks to the island and the kitchen sink was pretty spacious and and the faucet powerful. It also had a solid amount of cabinets/drawers and a pantry.

The bathroom was modern and pretty spacious by NYC standards. Never had any issues with running out of hot water.

The video intercom was convenient for deliveries and visitors.

As far as amenities outside of the unit itself, there was roof access with a decent view and there is a bike room. There's also a (paid) parking garage.

There is a grocery store very close by which I liked a good amount. It was very spacious by NYC standards and literally never busy.

Management allowed me to do a month to month lease after my initial year ended and even gave me a few free extra days when I was moving to my new place. They were also very prompt in sending me back my security deposit. Cons: First off, the apartment was absolutely filthy when I moved in. For example, it literally took me a few weeks to realize my kitchen cabinets didn't match the marble counter pattern, they were just covered in dust and dirt.

The floors used some sort of cheap laminate panels. When I moved in I realized some of the panels were loose and damaged which I did not notice in my original tour. Management promised to fix but it never happened (although truthfully I didn't hound them too hard on this one). 

A huge complaint is the lack of sound insulation anywhere in my unit. I could hear my neighbors constantly from literally everywhere in the apartment. And vice versa, I think my neighbors could hear me (especially when I was using the bathroom which was located right next to the door). 

I also unfortunately had a neighbor that constantly allowed their kids to play and stomp up and down the hallway. A downstairs neighbor even came to my door and blamed me for the stomping at one point. I also constantly smelled weed smoke inside my apartment coming from one or more neighbors.

The amenities suck compared to pretty much every other new construction in the neighborhood. The agent who showed me the unit initially said a gym was in the works but later backtracked when I asked him about it. The "roof access" has a decent view BUT the HVAC units take up so much space and are so loud that it makes you not want to stay there at all.

There is essentially 1 elevator in the building (there's another elevator but it only goes to like 2 floors for some reason) and it's very slow and rickety. Honestly I sometimes worried getting in that thing. Also about halfway through the lease it started making a squealing noise which I could hear from inside my bedroom (which was adjacent to the elevator).

My washer and dryer broke halfway through the lease and it was like pulling teeth to get management to address the issue. Eventually they did replace them but it took 5 - 6 weeks with a long period of radio silence from management. One of the broken units was sitting in my living room after the first repair attempt. It was at this point that management ghosted me for several weeks. I literally thought they were never going to get back to me so I ended up pushing the broken unit into the hallway because it was taking up a big chunk of my living space. 

The building had a huge package theft problem. Packages were stolen on countless occasions. Management's "fix" was to tell us to report it to the police and to pick up packages ASAP. This was one of the main reasons I left.

Also, probably related to the above item but this new, "up and coming" neighborhood of Hallet's Cove is pretty close to the hood/projects. While I lived there, a few shootings actually occurred right down the road. One night I walked out of the local convenience store and witnessed a street fight breaking out with a big contingent of the locals cheering it on. I felt like I was in a worldstar video. When coming and going to my apartment, I generally tried to avoid going down 8th street at all costs (especially at night) and mostly stuck to 27th ave. I didn't feel safe in the neighborhood and never lingered outside.

Outside of the proximity to sketchy areas, Hallet's Cove is still pretty empty and desolate. At the time of writing, it's got the grocery store, an urgent care center, and a tiny convenience store. And the area is still massively under construction with several high rise buildings going up, probably for at least the next few years.

If I'm being honest, the current state of the neighborhood was probably my biggest reason for wanting to leave this building. I think this neighborhood has a lot of potential (it could become a miniature LIC) but it's going to take probably another 5 - 10 years at least to get there.

Pros: Good apartment sizes and balconies. It's the only pro. Cons: Apartment was dirty when moved in. I gave the management a list of items to address/clean before move in and almost none was done.  I got tired of following up.

Management is slow to respond to issues within the apartment. I have to threaten with no paying rent so they can be responsive every time.

Security is non-existent in this building. Pretty much anybody can walk in at any time. Amazon packages get stolen every single day. Construction workers leave the garage door open all the time. The main door opens by itself for no reason at all. There's no security key card at the door leading to the building from the garage. There's no security key card at the elevator for the residents leaving any body who walk into the retail space on the 2nd floor free to access the residences.

The door with the accessible ramp doesn't work at all. It is very inconvenient when walking in with strollers

There's no amenities whatsoever even though they were promised when moved in. No rooftop, no gym, nothing.

Storage rooms are unattended and things get stolen every time.

Pros: New construction, first move in. Brooklyn Harvest Supermarket two blocks proximity. Q18, Q19, Q103, & Q102 bus terminals nearby. 10 minute walk to ferry. Cons: Building is new but it has cracks everywhere. Bathroom fixtures are cheap. There is no response  (zero, nada) from management if something needs fixing. Building is unfinished in common areas. Some items in the apartment are breaking down too soon. Area is still in development, no foot traffic and empty buildings. Gym and roof deck were advertised but are not finished. The noise between floors is very loud. You can hear your neighbors walking. 

Update: After a year and a halve the building is still unfinished. A new business opened on the second floor that share the same entrance with the tenants, in which unknown people come in and out. Even when the building is nonsmoking, at least in my floor, you can smell weed coming into your apartment through the entrance door wind draft at all time. I have found the service door and garage door open late at night with no supervision.

Update 9/29/2023: The entrance of the building and some apartments get flooded when there is heavy rain.

Pros: Cheaper rent close to prospect park and the Q train Cons: Cheaply made/things break. Management difficult to deal with. Lots of noise from the street from cars honking. People smoking cigarettes indoors.

Pros: attached to a grocery store, gym was small but manageable, neighbors were kind or kept to themselves. Management was responsive when roof began leaking. No real issues Cons: Trash would pile up on weekends but no bugs/rodent (thankfully)

Pros: My apartment is nice and the building amenities are seemingly nice. Cons: Neighbors are disgusting, don’t know how to just a trash chute, constantly dealing with roaches. The rooftop is absolutely disgusting and unusable— tenants are constantly taking their animals up there to defecate. I had literal mold and roaches coming OUT OF MY AC UNIT. Building management is VERY SLOW to respond to any requests, they starting being responsive once I involved 311. Rent is too damn high, and the garage rate is insane.

Pros: Some units have massive amount of outdoor space. There's a gym, small but functional. Rooftop deck, parking, central air and digital doorman. You have washer and dryers unit, so some money saved. Large supermarket downstairs. Cons: The rent can run pretty high for the location. You are near a middle school, so you hear the kids outside during recess which, depending on what floor you're on, can be pretty annoying. Late night basketball games can get rather rowdy which, again based on what floor you're on, can cause irritation. The water pressure isn't as powerful as I would like it to be. 

People who don't live in the building can walk in and out sometimes if they can catch the door before it closes, so that kind of lessens the security especially in a not so safe area
Pros: Clean, modern, quiet  Cons: Landlord is not friendly, neighbors are generally nice, but some not, far from a lot of things.

Pros: Amenities location park Cons: Elevator issues, recoccuring bedbugs throughout building in last few years. When you look up 51sr/52nd St Tenants Corp you will see it's really METRO MANAGEMENT DEVELOPMENT INC. Read the endless 1* google & help reviews. Search address on Augmented to see bedbug and rat history

Pros: Super is on-site, building is cleaned semi-regularly, monthly exterminator visit Cons: The laundry downstairs does not work, the walkway into the building is frequently dirty. When I had a series of packages stolen (and others in the building did as well), the management company did nothing to help identify if the thief was internal or external.

Pros: elevator pretty reliable and 2 washers + 2 dryers working 99.9% of the time Cons: loose garbage will cover the walkway into our foyer for weeks before a neighbor is fed up enough & uses their own cleaning supplies to clean up the foyer. building rated as an F in energy efficiency and pests are persistent

Pros: Access to laundry in basement, friendly neighbors many long-term renters & owners  Cons: Owner doesn’t seem to care about the outside area / foyer being clean or tidy.. frequently riddled with garbage from messy neighbors and bar goers across the street, up to tenants to clean up if it bothers us

Pros: Management here is really nice and so responsive and I’ve ever had an issue with getting a hold of maintenance- everyone’s really on top of things like that. Clean buildings with a nice gym and small, well maintained pool in the summers. Cons: Courtyard can be loud if people aren’t using headphones but it isn’t often and people need to be reminded about the rules regarding pets here. The rooms are small with sliding doors.  Neighborhood isn’t ideal, especially with few bigger grocery stores nearby (if you don’t have a car at least).
Pros: Janitorial staff are great and keep the surrounding areas clean. Cons: Maintenance is not good at their job. I had water by my which caused mold and they just painted over it.
Pros: Amenities are decent Cons: The heat is none existent; you crank it up and still have a cold apartment and high electric bill.
Pros: Quiet, clean, and no complaints Cons: Wish the surrounding neighborhood was less rough
Pros: Clean, lots of amenities Cons: Neighborhood is a little rough-looking around the apartment complex

Pros: Really nice super who is willing to help you with things. Cons: Building management is evil. The heat in the building was hardly ever on and I had to threaten legal action just to get my security deposit back.

Pros: The super and handyman are very responsive and kind men. I had no interactions with the landlord (BLDG Management) though I did successfully receive my security deposit back, paid in full, without any problems. Cons: My next door neighbor sadly passed away while I was living there
Pros: Relatively quiet and reasonably clean Cons: Absolutely awful management, not willing to take any responsibility for issues, no sense of urgency
Pros: Friendly neighbors and great location Cons: Small apartments and slower maintenance

Pros: The location is amazing. So close to Central Park, restaurants and the subways. If you have small kids, the zoned elementary school is great. Cons: The management company was always difficult to get a hold of. We had 3 different super. One was great, the others made sure you knew they were displeased to have to fix anything.

Pros: Always spotless- building was cleaned often and never had any bugs. Whenever I had an issue (shower clogged once) it was immediately addressed. Super lives close by and all the guys who work in the building are lovely. Cons: Building management takes days, even weeks to respond. Never got back to me about rent negotiations. I severely overpaid for my studio.

Pros: Some nice neighbors, proximity to A train, good water pressure Cons: Freezing in the winter, they keep temp just borderline so you can’t file a complaint, but nights are really cold. Illegal construction work, super that doesn’t speak English hence can’t fix any issues you might have cause you can not communicate with him. Mice, roaches. Constant package theft. Noise from the street is pretty bad if your windows face 181st st. List can go in and on.

Pros: Absolutely none. Maybe that you’ll have a roof over your head if you rent here. That’s about it. Cons: Owner is shady, there’s construction all over the place without permits. They just converted a commercial space I to two apartments (!!!), construction causes dust and the whole building is powdery. Windows are old so it’s NOISY. You can hear people on the street having conversations from the 5th floor. 

THERE IS NO GAS. It’s been at least 10 months without gas. Owner expects you to cook with a cheap hot plate that granted, was provided, but broke after 3 weeks.

SUPER DOESN’T SPEAK ENGLISH. If you speak Albanian then good for you, you’ll be able to ask for help. Otherwise forget it. It’s like there’s no super whatsoever. His wife is the one that cleans and his kid (!!!!) sort the trash.

Pros: The super is great and is available often to fix things. He is the only person who is functional within the administration in this building. Cons: We haven’t had working gas for over a year, management is impossible to contact and when you happen to get a hold of them, they remove themselves from taking accountability for anything in regards to the state of the building. We also didn’t have working mail boxes for over 6 months. For both the gas and the mail, tenants had to collectively contact local government to get the attention of the property owner. Still, the property owner took no responsibility and now we are over a year with no gas for cooking, along with that, there has been no offer for rent reduction.

Pros: Quiet block, wide hallways and large apartments. Kind neighbors. Cons: The super is a ghost — phone calls and texts go unanswered for months. Good luck if you have issues with heat or a leak. Laundry room is hardly an amenity since it consistently smells like cat poop and the machines are dirty and out of order half the time. Garbage piled up on the stairs down to the courtyard making it dangerous to actually take out the trash. It took management over a week to fix the out-of-order elevator.

Pros: Thick walls, cheap laundry, quiet block Cons: Basement laundry room is full of cats and cat poop at all times. Elevator is slow and noisy. It beeped incessantly for 3 months straight during my tenancy and I could hear it from inside my unit. Super is not the most responsive

Pros: Elevator (that is out of service lots of the time though) Cons: Leaky/raining ceilings that the super / management company completely doesn’t care about. Ceilings caving in, cupboards falling off of walls, and increased pests (major cockroach infestation) as a result. Been happening for years and in multiple rooms. They never seem to care. In fact the day we had our worst ceiling leakage we received our rent increase letter in the mail. Incredible. Additionally any “attempt” at “repair” is usually just painting over the issue and not fixing plumbing/replace walls that are now molding. 
Terrible communication skills. Any time you may have an issue I wish you luck trying to get the super or management on the phone, and if you do they couldn’t make you feel like more of an inconvenience. 
There was an instance where the front door buzzer/keyhole wasn’t working and their answer was to leave it propped open for weeks so that anyone off the street could make it into our building 24/7. Felt nice and safe.

Pros: - close to transportation, including the highway
- plenty of stores and restaurants 
- near the park and hospital Cons: Terrible unresponsive management! My partner and I first moved here in May of 2021. The day we moved, we should have known this was going to be a rollercoaster. As we were moving furniture, there was a birthday party which included guests, chairs, birthday cake, goodie bags, and a gift table. An event is happening in the hallway while people are moving. The building super was contacted and immediately stated that he couldn't do anything about it. Months later, our bathroom ceiling got molded, so we contacted the super and management. They [the building manager and super] were very dismissive in supporting their tenants, and it took them over two months to respond to our request. In June of 2022, our refrigerator broke down, we called management and the super to get it repaired, and again, they were never available. Within days our groceries were rotting, melting, and not lasting. Calling the management daily for support didn't work. We heard from the manager two weeks later, the day after we placed a 311 complaint. 

In July 2022, the mold from the bathroom ceiling reappeared over the newly patched work. After months of contacting the office, a third-party contractor visited the apartment and informed us that there was leakage from upstairs. That same day he called the building super, and as usual, the building super said, "I'll look at it later," but never appeared. He advised us to call the landlord in regards to sending a plumber, but in the meantime, he would temporarily patch it again. Since July 2022, we've placed ten 311 complaints regarding our unsanitary living conditions [holes in the ceiling, mold, and sewage problems/ blockage] due to maintenance. The building manager has been contacted daily but doesn't respond to support, as "he's never available" unless he gets the 311 calls from the Department of Housing.  

We advise you to save your money! The building is filthy, barely moped, piles of garbage are stacked in the entryway of the basement, and no one [suoer, manager, or the tenants] tries to resolve this hazardous problem. No one should pay about $2000 a month to live with excessive mold on the bathroom ceiling and experience daily sewage problems/ blockage since 2021. The building manager and super [who lives in the building] are either never available, are off/ vacation, get an attitude when discussing the unsanitary living conditions of our apartment, or they'll say they'll visit the apartment, we take a day off, for them to never appear. We've lived in this building for over one year and have placed multiple 311 complaints due to negligence.

Pros: The building is near a park and steps away from public transportation and the Henry Hudson highway. Cons: Not as clean as it should be (literally walked around a soda stain near my door from Monday to Thursday). 
Noise in hallways, in fact when I moved into the building (the literal FIRST DAY I began moving in, there was  an entire birthday party in the lobby. 

The building manager barely exists. I've never met him, despite telling me he would come to look at the mold that's been in my bathroom ceiling for a year (and growing to this day) I have no idea what he looks like, frankly, I'm not sure if its the manager when I'm on the phone. I pay close to $2000 a month to be ignored by the super (he literally put his head down when he saw my wife and I) and the garbage...oh boy! The garbage management is HORRIFIC!! The tenants are allowed to put the garbage in the staircase to the basement. So.etimes the building cats do their part by eating the garbage
311 will know your first name if you move here..matter of fact,. 
DO NOT MOVE HERE! IF YOU LOVE YOUR FRIENDS OR FAMILY DONT LET THEM MOVE HERE! IF YOU HAVE A CONSCIENCE AND BREATH AIR, DONT LET ANYONE MOVE HERE!!!
